title: step applies commands one-by-one instead of the arch §11.1 pinned topology_apply_all atomic batch (E23)
detail: A failing command in a batch leaves earlier commands applied (partial batch); only a corrupt log can reach it today (defined rejection), so latent — but E27 junction-demolish pins atomic validate-all-then-apply, which this loop lacks.
recommended_fix: Add core::topology_apply_all (validate all, then apply) per §6.1/E23 and call it from step; keep per-command topology_apply_edit for the app fast-path.

title: E4 snap uses a float world-px metric in the app, not the arch §6.1 pinned integer metric; the E4 unit test pins a metric the snap path never uses
evidence:
app/main.odin:153-167: "radius := f32(app.cat.balance.snap_radius)
	r2 := f64(radius) * f64(radius)" ... "nx := f32(t.node_pos[i][0]) * tile" ... "d2 := dx*dx + dy*dy" — vs core/topology_test.odin:122: "testing.expect(t, dist2({0, 0}, {36, 0}) <= 36*36, \"snap must be inclusive at the radius boundary (E4)\")" — a TILE-coordinate dist2 test (36 = the px radius used as a tile distance), and arch §6.1: "One metric serves span validation, draw cost (length × tier), and the snap radius (E4)."
detail: The arch's one-metric claim is split: core validates in integer tiles, snap resolves in f64 world px. Determinism is safe (log stores post-snap ids), but the real E4 snap is untested and the named E4 test exercises different math.
recommended_fix: Either pin the app snap against the core metric (convert px→tiles, use dist2) or rename the test and add a snap_node unit test; document the two-metric split in §6.1.

title: round-half-up span accepts true lengths up to max_span+0.5, deviating from the arch §6.1 pinned d² <= span² compare
detail: The integer isqrt is exact and deterministic, but rounding down at the half boundary accepts spans up to 0.5 tile over the tier cap — the arch pinned the strict squared compare. No current fixture/data hits the boundary.
recommended_fix: Pin the boundary: either compare d2 <= max_span² in validate_draw (rounded span kept for cost display only) or add a test documenting the +0.5 acceptance and update §6.1.

title: ODN-5 unknown-field fail-fast is claimed in the header comment but not implemented; lb_mode_capable is silently ignored
evidence: catalog.odin:4: "// loaded once, fail-fast validated (unknown fields, out-of-range values," — but the loader only reads known keys: "nt.terminal_role = role_from_name(jstr(eo, \"terminal_role\"))" (catalog.odin:108) and never rejects unknown ones; data/node_types.json:10 carries "lb_mode_capable": false, which Node_Type (catalog.odin:32-39) has no field for — parsed and dropped silently. Arch ODN-5: "Load-time validation is fail-fast: unknown fields, out-of-range values, cross-reference errors ... abort startup with a named error."
detail: A typo'd/renamed catalog field is silently ignored instead of aborting, violating the ODN-5 fail-fast contract the comment promises; catalog_hash still binds bytes, so no silent sim divergence.
recommended_fix: After parsing each entry, walk the JSON object and error on any key not consumed; drop or consume lb_mode_capable explicitly.

title: Demos lower to Commands directly, bypassing the app's Input Layer / Command_Bus — arch §10.3's same-path-as-a-mouse contract is not met
detail: The app's snap/drag path (E4, E3-at-bus, drag semantics) never runs in CI — app.bin only compiles (ci.yml:74 "Game builds (app.bin compiles + links)"). T2 verifies render+topology, not the app wiring. Determinism is unaffected (log stores resolved ids).
recommended_fix: For 1.3+, route demos through an intent→command layer shared with the app (or a headless snap proc in core), so the input path is CI-exercised; document the 1.2 command-level deviation in §10.3.

title: load_catalogs/seed_fixture duplication is acceptable per-layer IO, but the app's fixture is unguarded literals with no cross-verification
detail: Core purity (ODN-1) makes per-executable loaders the right call, and catalog_hash binds divergence loudly — but if the app fixture ever drifts from the harness's, the app's on-screen map silently differs from the blessed T2 frame and no gate catches it.
recommended_fix: Keep the duplication (it is correct), but have the app read fixture positions from the same named constants/JSON the harness uses, or add an app-side smoke check against the blessed frame.
